**The match is a 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 32 knockout fixture between Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire) and Norway, scheduled for June 30, 2026, at Dallas Stadium (AT&T Stadium) in Arlington, Texas (Dallas area), with kickoff at 12:00 p.m. local/ET (17:00 in Yamoussoukro, 19:00 in Oslo).**[[1]](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/cote-divoire-norway-live-stream-team-news-tickets)[[2]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/06/27/opening-odds-for-ivory-coast-vs-norway-in-the-fifa-2026-world-cup/)

Key factors beyond raw team strength (drawn only from information available before June 27, 2026) include:

**Head-to-head history**: Public previews and stats pages provide limited or no detailed historical meetings between the senior teams in major tournaments or otherwise. They secured their Round of 32 spot with a win in their final Group E match against Curaçao.[[2]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/06/27/opening-odds-for-ivory-coast-vs-norway-in-the-fifa-2026-world-cup/)[[5]](https://www.cbssports.com/watch/soccer/video/ivory-coast-vs-norway-world-cup-r32-preview-norway-look-to-make-history-48-nations) Norway finished second in Group I (behind France), having used backups in their final group match and boasting a strong qualifying campaign (perfect record in European qualifiers, first major tournament appearance since Euro 2000).[[2]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/06/27/opening-odds-for-ivory-coast-vs-norway-in-the-fifa-2026-world-cup/)[[6]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/07/norway-world-cup-2026-team-guide)

**Injuries/suspensions to key players**: Ivory Coast’s 26-man squad (announced around mid-May 2026) saw changes due to injury: Sébastien Haller was omitted; defender Clément Akpa (adductor issue at club) was replaced by Christopher Operi; Franck Kessié had an injury scare at club level but was included; Evann Guessand had been sidelined since early April.[[7]](https://africa.espn.com/football/story/_/id/48778996/ivory-coast-2026-world-cup-squad-sebastien-haller-ange-yoan-bonny)[[8]](https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/operi-gets-world-cup-call-up-injury-replacement-2026-05-30/)[[9]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/ivory-coast-2026-world-cup-040000062.html) Norway’s squad featured Erling Haaland (strong qualifying form with 16 goals noted in profiles) and captain Martin Ødegaard, with no prominent pre-match injury reports highlighted in available previews.[[10]](https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/02a6-20d1592b3f90-2ef16e2c5255-1000--norway-at-the-world-cup-2026-squad-fixtures-group-and-hi/)[[11]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/norway-2026-world-cup-squad-112500124.html)

**Travel distance/fatigue and venue conditions**: Both teams were based in or traveling within North America for the tournament. Ivory Coast held a pre-tournament training camp in Paris before heading to the US. The match was at the indoor, climate-controlled AT&T Stadium (FIFA capacity ~94,000 for the event), avoiding outdoor extremes. Outside conditions were expected to be hot and humid (low-to-mid 90s°F / ~33–35°C), but irrelevant inside. The venue is flat (no altitude issues).[[12]](https://bolavip.com/en/world-cup/in-which-city-and-stadium-are-ivory-coast-vs-norway-playing-today-weather-attendance-for-wc-game)[[2]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/06/27/opening-odds-for-ivory-coast-vs-norway-in-the-fifa-2026-world-cup/) Norway supporters were noted traveling and creating a visible presence (“Viking Row”).[[13]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U8NM0aYENsc)

**Crowd/home advantage and other storylines**: Neutral US venue with no strong home advantage for either side, though Norway fans were highlighted as bringing notable atmosphere and numbers. Ivory Coast’s storyline centered on making history by reaching the knockout rounds for the first time. Norway aimed to build on their return to a major tournament with star forward Haaland in strong form. Pre-match betting odds (as of June 27) made Norway slight favorites (moneyline around +105, Ivory Coast +265 to win, draw +250), with Norway favored to advance.[[2]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/06/27/opening-odds-for-ivory-coast-vs-norway-in-the-fifa-2026-world-cup/)[[2]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/06/27/opening-odds-for-ivory-coast-vs-norway-in-the-fifa-2026-world-cup/)

These elements (neutral indoor venue, Ivory Coast’s historic breakthrough vs. Norway’s experience and star power, squad tweaks from injuries, and limited prior meetings) were the primary talking points in pre-match coverage. No major suspensions or extreme travel/fatigue issues were flagged beyond standard tournament demands.

factors.impact: Significant negative for Ivory Coast. The confirmed omission of key striker Sébastien Haller and defender Clément Akpa due to injury, alongside an injury scare for Franck Kessié, directly impacts their squad strength, particularly in crucial attacking and defensive roles.

factors.factor: Norway's key player health and form
factors.impact: Positive for Norway. Star forward Erling Haaland, highlighted for his 16 goals in qualifying, and captain Martin Ødegaard are both reported fit and in strong form, ensuring their primary attacking and creative outlets are fully available and effective.

factors.factor: Norway's recent form and squad management
factors.impact: Positive for Norway. Their perfect record in European qualifiers demonstrates consistent high performance. The strategic use of backups in their final group stage match suggests either a comfortable qualification position or successful squad rotation to keep key players fresh, which is an advantage for a knockout match.

Positive for Ivory Coast. Reaching the World Cup knockout stage for the first time is a significant morale booster and could inspire a highly motivated performance, though this is primarily a psychological factor.

Neutral for both teams. The match being held in an indoor, climate-controlled stadium (AT&T Stadium) negates any potential impact from external weather conditions (heat/humidity), and both teams' presence within North America reduces unique travel or fatigue disadvantages.
Slight positive for Norway. As of June 27, betting markets indicate Norway as slight favorites to win and advance, providing external corroboration for their perceived stronger position.

analysis.reasoning: The data suggests a discernible lean towards Norway. While Ivory Coast's historic qualification for the knockout stage undoubtedly provides a morale boost, this is offset by concrete squad disadvantages. The confirmed absence of key striker Sébastien Haller and defender Clément Akpa due to injury, coupled with an injury scare for Franck Kessié, significantly weakens Ivory Coast's tactical options and overall strength. In contrast, Norway's crucial players, notably Erling Haaland (with his prolific 16 qualifying goals) and captain Martin Ødegaard, are reported to be in strong form and free of prominent injury concerns. Norway's perfect record in European qualifiers speaks to a high level of consistent performance, and their ability to utilize backups in their final group match indicates either superior depth or strategic player management for this critical knockout tie. Head-to-head history is negligible, and the neutral, climate-controlled venue negates external environmental factors or significant travel fatigue for either side. The pre-match betting odds also align with Norway being slight favorites, further supporting their stronger standing based on current form and squad health.
